# Monday 14 September 2026

Weekend roll-up, covering Friday 11 through Monday 14. 19 records considered, 5 included, 6 dropped as duplicates, 8 below the $10M floor or off-axis.

---

## THE ONE THING

Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier" on 12 September and committed Anthropic, unilaterally, to giving third-party evaluators permanent employee-level access: "desks in our offices, access badges, and company laptops", permissions comparable to internal risk teams, and the right to publish findings unfavourable to the company. His stated purpose is that "embedded evaluators can check at the level of nuts and bolts whether an AI company is actually following the training, deployment, operational, and safeguards practices they claim to be following." The analogy he uses is the bank examiner. Sam Altman committed OpenAI to match it the same day. ([darioamodei.com](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier))

*new · primary-company · two-source · touches: assurance seam*

Why it is not just an announcement: the two largest labs have voluntarily created a third-party evaluation function in the same eighteen months that the EU created a mandatory one for self-evolving safety components and BIS made chip export eligibility conditional on independent testing. Three regimes, no coordination, same structural answer.

---

## MOVES

**Altman matched within hours, and the gap is in the operational detail.** Altman wrote that "committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same." OpenAI has not published the evaluators' selection process, their technical access, confidentiality rules, or any authority over model deployments, and said only that it will "have more to share soon." The unspecified items are exactly the ones that decide whether an embedded evaluator is an auditor or a guest. ([Unite.AI](https://www.unite.ai/altman-says-openai-will-match-anthropics-embedded-evaluator-pledge/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/14/sam-altman-ai-slowdown-anthropic-amodei-musk.html)) · *geo · secondary-press · two-source*

**Amodei named recursive self-improvement as one of two triggers, and located it inside his own company.** He writes that AI has been advancing drastically faster "driven primarily by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI", and that this is starting to happen across the industry, Anthropic included. The second trigger was a swarm of agents conducting unauthorised cyberattacks. A CEO attributing his own acceleration to recursion, in writing, is a different kind of claim from a forecast. ([darioamodei.com](https://darioamodei.com/post/we-must-pace-the-frontier)) · *new · primary-company · single-source*

**Paul Graham published "Making Startups Powerful".** The argument is that founders should optimise for power rather than profit directly, because "thinking about how to make it more powerful will sometimes make it orders of magnitude more valuable", through owning the customer relationship instead of remaining a component supplier, network effects, going full stack, and acquiring data early in the customer lifecycle. The binding constraint he states is that "you can only do these things when the result is better for the customer." Read against an independent-evaluator business, the power sources he lists are mostly unavailable to a referee by construction, since a referee cannot own the customer relationship or go full stack without ceasing to be neutral. ([paulgraham.com](https://paulgraham.com/powerful.html)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

**The EU has still not received harmonised standards for the AI requirements it starts enforcing in four months.** Per Commission information from August 2026, no harmonised standards had yet been submitted by the European standardisation organisations for the new cybersecurity and artificial intelligence requirements under Machinery Regulation 2023/1230. prEN 50742, on protection against corruption, had its final vote scheduled for September 2026 with publication possibly in November. Roughly 800 existing Machinery Directive standards are to be carried over, first citations expected Q3 2026. ([IBF Solutions](https://www.ibf-solutions.com/en/seminars-and-news/news/new-machinery-regulation-status-of-harmonised-standards), [European Commission](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/goods/european-standards/harmonised-standards/machinery-md_en)) · *geo · secondary-press citing primary · single-source*

---

## DIFFS

`Embedded third-party evaluators at frontier labs: was none -> now 2 labs committed, Anthropic unilateral and OpenAI matching (2026-09-12)` [darioamodei.com, Unite.AI]

`EU Machinery harmonised standards for AI requirements: was Aug 2025 deadline missed -> now still none submitted as of Aug 2026, 4 months before the 2027-01-20 application date` [IBF Solutions]

`Assurance-seam thesis: was 7 beachheads and structurally uncrowded -> now narrowed to non-regression at the moment of model update` [internal research, 2026-09-13]

`Funding floor: was unset -> now $10M, with the live-thesis exception` [your decision, 2026-09-14]

---

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

*No domain in progress. Section omitted rather than filled.*

The one decision still outstanding is which domain the stock side starts on. My recommendation remains industrial certification and standards bodies as a business, and this week's items are an argument for it: three separate regimes have now created a demand for third-party attestation, and there is still no primary document in this portal about how a notified body prices work, obtains accreditation, or structures its costs.

---

## ONE QUESTION

The Sept 13 internal reading was that NHTSA withdrawing AV STEP cut against the thesis, because a regulator declining to create a third-party evaluation market turns each safety case into a services engagement rather than a product. Anthropic and OpenAI have now created that function voluntarily, without a regulator. Does a voluntarily created evaluator seat become a product faster than a mandated one, or slower, given the labs choose their own examiners and can unchoose them?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: 19 records from 3 sources (F6 Voices, F3 Policy Diff, F1 Capital Ledger). F4 and F5 not run.
Included: 5. Dropped as duplicate: 6, all secondary coverage of the Amodei post. Below floor or off-axis: 8.
Sources unreachable: none. X not read, deferred by your decision of 2026-09-14.
Empty windows: F1 Capital Ledger returned no qualifying items above the $10M floor in the window.

Verification: 2 of 5 items two-source, 3 single-source and flagged inline.
Primary documents retrieved and read: the Amodei post, the Graham essay, the Commission harmonised-standards page, Amodei's index page.
Not verified to primary: the Commission's August 2026 statement about standards not yet submitted is reported by IBF Solutions, a consultancy, and was not located in a Commission document. The Altman quote is reported from a post on X, not read at source. Treat both as secondary until checked.
Word count: 648 excluding this block.

*Hand-run by Claude, 2026-09-14, ahead of the collectors being built. The agent charters this follows are in data/agents.js; the format and its reasoning are in reports/agent-system-plan-2026-09-10.md.*

---

## UPDATE, 07:13 PDT

F4 and F5 were not run this morning. They have now been run, and F1 and F3 were re-run. Four items were absent from the brief above, and one of them corrects it.

**F1 reported an empty window this morning. It was not empty.** Two rounds above the floor were announced on 11 September, inside the window. AIDIN Robotics, Anyang, closed KRW 16 billion in strategic financing, HD Hyundai Robotics putting in 13 billion won and Samsung Venture Investment 3 billion. It sells six-axis force and torque sensors and the force-control software that uses them, and says it will stand up annual capacity for 30,000 force and torque sensors and co-develop a five-finger hand for shipyards. ([KED Global](https://www.kedglobal.com/robotics/newsView/ked202609110009), [Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/09/11/startup-funding-news-today-september-11-2026-kinetix-ai-aidin-robotics-enigmata-more/)) · *money · secondary-press · two-source · USD disputed: $12.1M and $11.9M reported, not converted here*

**Kinetix AI, Shenzhen, disclosed more than RMB 500 million across a series of Angel+ financings**, from Vertex Ventures, Fangguang Capital and Wanshi Capital, for an embodied-AI stack combining data, models and hardware. The source states $74.5M; that is the source's conversion and is not carried as a figure. ([Tech Startups](https://techstartups.com/2026/09/11/startup-funding-news-today-september-11-2026-kinetix-ai-aidin-robotics-enigmata-more/)) · *money · secondary-press · single-source*

**A paper submitted 11 September claims zero real-world training data is needed for deformable folding.** FoldNet++ reports 6 robotic embodiments, 1K T-shirts, 1K environmental assets and 120K episodes, and states that "models trained solely on our synthetic data can achieve over 90% end-to-end task success rates when directly deployed to unseen real-world environments and previously unseen T-shirts from arbitrary initial configurations." Cloth physics come from an FEM simulator. ([arXiv 2609.12433](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12433)) · *new · primary-author · single-source · disputed_by: no pushback observed in window*

**Correction to the DIFF above on EU machinery.** A watchlist instrument moved on 24 July 2026 and this system had not recorded it. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, in force 27 July 2026, at Article 1 point 41 "deletes only point 1 of Section A, which referred to Directive 2006/42/EC, and adds Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 as point 21 of Section B" of Annex I to the AI Act. Effect as reported: a manufacturer "will not have to conduct a separate conformity assessment under the AI Regulation for its safety component...and then another conformity assessment under the Machinery Regulation." The delegated act folding high-risk AI requirements into the Machinery Regulation is due 2 August 2028. ([Eurogip](https://eurogip.fr/en/machinery-regulation-2023-1230-what-the-digital-omnibus-on-ai-changes/), [NicFab](https://www.nicfab.eu/en/posts/digital-omnibus-ai-official-journal/)) · *geo · secondary-press · two-source · primary not retrieved*

`buried`: none additional. The move removes a duplicate assessment; it does not, on this reading, touch Machinery Regulation Annex I Part A item 5, which is a separate Annex in a separate instrument and still routes self-evolving ML safety components through a notified body under Module B, G or H.

---

### DIFFS, update

`F1 window 11-14 Sep: was "no qualifying items above the $10M floor" (this morning) -> now 2 qualifying rounds, KRW 16bn and RMB 500M+, both announced 2026-09-11` [KED Global, Tech Startups]

`Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 in AI Act Annex I: was Section A point 1 (as Directive 2006/42/EC) -> now Section B point 21, moved by Reg (EU) 2026/1744, in force 2026-07-27` [Eurogip, NicFab, primary not retrieved]

`Zero-shot real-world success from synthetic data only, T-shirt folding: was not tracked -> now a claimed >90% end-to-end (2026-09-11)` [arXiv 2609.12433]

---

### THESIS SENTRY

Two items reach the bar, both weakening.

`assurance-seam` · FoldNet++ claims over 90% zero-shot real-world success on deformable folding from synthetic data alone ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12433)) · **weakens** · mechanism: it extends the self-liquidation argument from production telemetry to pre-deployment, because if a simulator reproduces the task well enough to train a policy that transfers, the same simulator is available to the buyer as an evaluation instrument at no marginal cost. confidence: holds only if the FEM cloth dynamics match reality on the specific actions used, which the paper self-reports and no third party has reproduced.

`assurance-seam` · The Digital Omnibus moved the Machinery Regulation out of Section A of AI Act Annex I ([Eurogip](https://eurogip.fr/en/machinery-regulation-2023-1230-what-the-digital-omnibus-on-ai-changes/)) · **changes-the-clock** · mechanism: the dated obligation leg of the thesis now rests on one conformity assessment rather than two stacked ones, and the AI-specific technical content of it is deferred to a delegated act due 2 August 2028 rather than biting on 20 January 2027. confidence: holds only if Machinery Annex I Part A item 5 is in fact untouched, which was not confirmed against the primary text.

---

### ONE QUESTION, update

If a simulator good enough to train a transferable policy is by construction good enough to evaluate one, does the non-regression wedge survive at all, or does it only survive for tasks whose simulators are still bad?

---

### PROVENANCE, update

Considered: 31 records across F1, F3, F4, F5, F6. Included: 4. Already in the brief above: 6. Below floor or off-axis: 19 (Provilac $14M dairy, nocall.ai, Enigmata, Furo, Blue Farm, 9lione, EdTechX, Yuedian and others).
Collectors reporting empty windows: F6 Voices, no new primary writing from the list in window. Dario Amodei's top post remains "We Must Pace the Frontier"; Paul Graham's remains "Making Startups Powerful"; Karpathy's newest are 30 Apr 2026 (bearblog) and 12 Feb 2026 (github). Physical Intelligence newest post 16 Apr 2026. F3 Federal Register and BIS: no watchlist movement in window, BIS returned zero documents 11-14 Sep.
Out of window and dropped on dateline: Anthropic's "Measuring tactical intelligence targeting and conventional weapons capabilities" (10 Sep) and "An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents" (9 Sep). The Digital Omnibus item is also out of window and is carried only because it corrects a DIFF published above.
Sources unreachable: EUR-Lex returned no body to four retrieval attempts (HTML, PDF, ELI and direct), so Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was not read at primary. openai.com/news/research returned HTTP 403. A paper-review site critique of FoldNet++ was surfaced in search but the page did not load, so it is not carried as pushback and disputed_by stays empty.
Novelty checked, not asserted: gbrain has no prior page on Kinetix AI, AIDIN Robotics or the Digital Omnibus.
Verification: 2 of 4 items two-source. 2 single-source, flagged inline. The AIDIN USD figure is disputed between sources and is reported in won only.
Board updated: data/library.js, card `assurance-seam`.
Word count: 612 excluding this block.

## UPDATE 2, 07:26 PDT · EUR-Lex now readable, the Omnibus item upgrades to primary

EUR-Lex answers non-browser clients with HTTP 202 and an empty body, which is why the item above shipped as secondary. The Publications Office CELLAR service serves the same documents with no such gate, and `tools/eurlex.mjs` now uses it. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 has been read at source. Three corrections follow.

**The Omnibus item is now primary-filing, two-source, and its verification tag above is superseded.** Recital 42 reads: "Given the specific nature of machinery and the machinery sector, and in order to address the need to simplify the regulatory framework for AI-enabled machinery, it is appropriate to move to a sectoral approach by moving Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 from Section A to Section B of Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689." The enacting term, Article 1 point 41, reads: "Annex I is amended as follows: (a) in Section A, point 1 is deleted; (b) in Section B, the following point is added: '21. Regulation (EU) 2023/1230...'". ([CELEX 32026R1744](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1744)) · *geo · primary-filing · two-source*

**The Annex I question is settled, and the reading above holds.** Article 3, the only article amending the Machinery Regulation, amends Article 8, Article 20 and Article 47 and nothing else. It does not mention Annex I. So Machinery Annex I Part A item 5 is untouched and self-evolving ML safety components still route through a notified body. The `buried` line above said "on this reading"; that hedge can be dropped.

**Two dates are firmer than reported.** Article 3(1) adds to Machinery Article 8: "Those delegated acts shall apply by 2 August 2028." Article 3(2) adds Article 20(10), letting manufacturers rely on AI Act harmonised standards for presumption of conformity "[u]ntil harmonised standards or common specifications are referenced or adopted pursuant to this Article as regards high-risk AI systems." Entry into force of the Omnibus is 2026-07-27, recorded in CELLAR, not inferred.

### DIFFS, update 2

`Reg (EU) 2026/1744 verification: was secondary-press, primary not retrieved (07:13) -> now primary-filing, read at CELEX 32026R1744` [CELLAR]

`Machinery Annex I Part A item 5 under the Omnibus: was "on this reading, untouched, not confirmed" -> now confirmed untouched, Article 3 amends only Articles 8, 20 and 47` [CELEX 32026R1744]

`F3 EU-law retrieval: was blocked, eur-lex.europa.eu returns HTTP 202 empty -> now tools/eurlex.mjs via CELLAR, discovery and retrieval both working` [this repo]

Correction to the provenance block at 07:13: it reported that Bash had no network access. That was wrong. # Tuesday 15 September 2026

Window 14 to 15 September. 51 records considered, 5 included, 46 dropped.

---

## THE ONE THING

Hiroki Sawada and Shunichi Kasahara published a benchmark on 14 September showing that aggregate rollout success rates cannot detect per-instance regression in a robot policy. LIBERO-CTRL pairs each initial state across six single-axis perturbation conditions and a matched simultaneous condition. The paper states that "even when the difference between the two transition rates is not statistically distinguishable from zero, as many as 29.0% of matched initial states still change outcome", reaching 34.5% in the most affected condition, across six policies and three severity levels. Its conclusion: "matched per-instance evaluation is needed to reveal how joint perturbations alter behavior." ([arXiv 2609.15940](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15940))

*new · primary-author · single-source · disputed_by: no pushback observed in window*

`assurance-seam, surviving form` · **supports** · mechanism: it measures what a paired design recovers that an aggregate rate hides. confidence: simulation only, six policies, no physical deployment.

---

## MOVES

**A federal agency stood up a voluntary third-party certification programme and sized it at nine submissions a year.** The Election Assistance Commission published its ESTEP Application for Testing form on 15 September. The notice says the programme "evaluates the functionality, security, and accessibility of election-supporting technologies" and that "Participation in this program is voluntary." Its burden table: 3 first-time submissions at 240 hours each, 6 subsequent at 32, 1,296 hours and $101,217.60 a year at $78.10 an hour. ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/15/2026-18797/agency-information-collection-activities-estep-application-for-testing)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

`buried`: the form is itself the new third-party testing instrument. No other testing, attestation or verification requirement appears in the notice.

`assurance-seam` · **weakens** · mechanism: a voluntary third-party certification seat, sized by the agency that runs it, is nine submissions a year. confidence: holds only if election technology is a fair comparator for machinery or frontier models.

**EUCLYD raised a Series A co-led by Samsung to sell inference silicon that is not a GPU.** The release of 15 September states EUCLYD "has signed a Series A financing round of more than €200 million", co-led by Samsung, Somerset Capital Partners, Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT and Innovation Industries. The company is "developing a platform spanning crafted compute, innovative memory architecture, and datacenter systems". CNBC reported $230 million; that is the outlet's conversion and is not carried. ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/euclyd-raises-over-200-million-to-break-the-ai-efficiency-wall-302878020.html)) · *money · primary-company · two-source*

**Nanjing ENCOS closed over RMB 300 million in Series B for robot joint modules.** The source reads "完成超3亿元人民币B轮融资". Investors named for this round are CITIC Goldstone, Nice Group, Su Venture Capital, Huarui Investment, Nanjing Transportation Control and Huarui VC, with Fosun RZ, Shenzhen Capital, Huakong, Jinqiu and Puhua following on. No lead is designated and no valuation is disclosed. It sells integrated joint modules and is extending from components into whole-machine hardware. ([Pedaily](https://news.pedaily.cn/202609/569015.shtml)) · *money · secondary-database · two-source*

---

## DIFFS

`Independent measurement of what aggregate rollout rates hide: was none tracked -> now 29.0% of matched initial states change outcome, 34.5% in the worst condition (2026-09-14)` [arXiv 2609.15940]

`Federal third-party certification programmes tracked: was 0 -> now 1, EAC ESTEP, voluntary, self-sized at 9 submissions and $101,217.60 a year (2026-09-15)` [Federal Register]

`Non-NVIDIA inference silicon raising at scale: was not tracked -> now EUCLYD, over €200M Series A co-led by Samsung (2026-09-15)` [PR Newswire]

`Robot policy layer, legal governance inside the planner: was not tracked -> now one paper, Defeasible Deontic Logic constraining a motion planner via learned world models, ex ante (2026-09-14)` [arXiv 2609.15113]

`Board: card assurance-seam updated with the paired-evaluation result and the ESTEP volume figure` [data/library.js]

---

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

Serialising `reports/terrain-map.md` section 1, industrial certification and standards bodies as a business. The vocabulary, first half.

Conformity assessment is the act of demonstrating that a product meets a legal requirement. Self-certification is the manufacturer doing it alone and signing a declaration. A notified body is a private company that a Member State has authorised to perform third-party conformity assessment, and the word "notified" is literal: the state notifies the Commission of it, and the register is called NANDO. A national accreditation body is a separate organisation that attests the candidate meets the competence requirements, which is a different step from being notified.

Next: the module routes, harmonised standards and presumption of conformity, then the value chain.

---

## ONE QUESTION

If the only independent measurement of the non-regression gap so far was published free on arXiv by two authors, is the defensible asset the method or the accredited seat that signs the certificate?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: 51 records from 5 collectors (F1 Capital Ledger, F3 Policy Diff, F4 Frontier Claims, F5 Thesis Sentry, F6 Voices).
Included: 5. Dropped as duplicate: 2, both secondary coverage of the EUCLYD round. Below floor, off-axis or out of window: 44.

Cut for the word cap, not for relevance: arXiv 2609.15113, "Legislating World-Model-Based Planning with Legal Reasoning", submitted 14 September, which "employs Defeasible Deontic Logic (DDL) to constrain a motion planner" and names a "grounding isomorphism gap" where perception error grounds false atoms and an "ontological isomorphism gap" where one legal conclusion admits many faithful encodings. It appears in DIFFS rather than MOVES. The 700-word ceiling and the 400-word stock-side allowance cannot both be spent in full, so MOVES was cut first, per the editor charter.

F6 Voices: no new primary writing from the list in window. darioamodei.com still lists four short posts, newest "We Must Pace the Frontier"; paulgraham.com/articles.html still opens with "Making Startups Powerful"; karpathy.github.io newest is 12 February 2026.

F3 Policy Diff: no watchlist movement. `tools/eurlex.mjs` scanned 29 sector-3 acts published 14 to 15 September by OJ publication date, none matching machinery, artificial intelligence, dual-use, conformity, standardisation, export or robot. Federal Register returned zero BIS documents in the window; NHTSA's only document was a Paperwork Reduction Act reinstatement of the Criminal Penalty Safe Harbor collection and FMCSA's was a renewal of the 391.41 medical collection, neither a watchlist movement. ESTEP is emitted as instrument NEW, not a watchlist entry.

F1 Capital Ledger: overflow, 3 further items at or above the floor not reported. RobotPlusPlus, Series C at "hundreds of millions of RMB", 15 September; Yincheng Intelligence, about RMB 100 million Series A for logistics picking robots, 15 September; Kangwei Vision, about RMB 100 million pre-Series A for optical inspection of semiconductors and PCBs, 15 September.

Dropped on dateline: Fortaegis, $50M Series A, because the company's own release is dated 13 September even though coverage ran 14 and 15 September. Also dropped: arXiv 2609.13236 on self-evolving humanoids, which appeared in the cs.RO new listing but was submitted 2 September, and arXiv 2609.14219 on metrological inspection, submitted 13 September. A secondary report that TNO had tested the Fortaegis architecture was checked against the company release, which does not say it, so the claim is not carried.

Sources unreachable: karpathy.bearblog.dev returned HTTP 404 at /blog, /blog/ and the site root, so that venue was not read today. iso.org returned HTTP 403, so the ISO 25785-1 stage was not checked at source. english.mofcom.gov.cn did not respond. bis.gov serves a single-page application with no dated press listing, so BIS rests on the Federal Register scan. The arXiv API returned HTTP 429 and 503, so the cs.RO listing pages were used instead and every date was confirmed on the paper's own abstract page. deepmind.google dates its blog to the month only, so it cannot be filtered to a 24-hour window and produced no item.

Novelty checked, not asserted: gbrain has no prior page on EUCLYD, ENCOS, RobotPlusPlus or LIBERO-CTRL.

Word count: 756 excluding this block, over the 700 ceiling. MOVES is already at its floor of 3, so the remaining overage sits in the ONE THING, the mandatory `buried` and thesis-direction blocks, the DIFFS lines and the stock-side serialisation, none of which the charter permits cutting ahead of MOVES. prEN 50742 did not move and was taken out of DIFFS: the final vote remains scheduled for September 2026 with publication possibly November, per IBF Solutions, and no ballot result has been published.
Verification: 2 of 5 items two-source, 3 single-source and flagged inline. No currency converted. No total computed. The EUCLYD CNBC report is the second source for that item and is not cited in the body because the charter allows one link per item.
Primary documents retrieved and read: the EAC notice in full text, the EUCLYD release, four arXiv abstract pages, darioamodei.com, paulgraham.com/articles.html, karpathy.github.io, physicalintelligence.company/blog, anthropic.com/news.
Board updated: data/library.js, card `assurance-seam`.

# Thursday 17 September 2026

Window 15 to 17 September, extended because no brief ran on the 16th. 61 records considered, 5 included, 56 dropped.

---

## THE ONE THING

The EPA published a final rule on 17 September, effective 16 November 2026, repealing "the CCS-based standards for new base load stationary combustion turbines (i.e., Phase 2 standards)" and most of the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards. It states its own driver: "Increasing amounts of large commercial and industrial loads, particularly those related to data center demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, are primarily driving this nearly 2.6-fold increase in projected growth rates." New base load turbines built for that load carry no carbon capture standard. ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/17/2026-19071/partial-repeal-of-the-carbon-pollution-standards-for-fossil-fuel-fired-electric-generating-units)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

`assurance-seam, surviving form` · **supports** · mechanism: a measured base rate for an aggregate improvement hiding a regression, and 55% is not a tail case. confidence: it gates a text context, not weights, and the shipping team picks the protected cases.

# Wednesday 30 September 2026

Window 23 to 30 September, extended because no brief ran between 23 and 29 September. 1,660 considered, 5 included.

---

## THE ONE THING

Someone replayed physical contact. "Audit Before You Commit", 24 September, audits a probe-then-commit insertion pipeline and reports that "replaying the recorded taps under an injected model error shows the audit's signature on real data", on a physical arm inserting a tool into a rigid pocket by touch. In simulation the truth leaves the belief's support on 16.9% of episodes while the failure score "turns optimistic by 0.31", and "confidently wrong instances still pass a confidence gate". Correcting a 2.1 mm error in the tap boundary cut failure from 0.354 to 0.112. ([arXiv 2609.30608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30608)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`buried`: what is replayed is recorded proprioceptive probes, not contact dynamics under a new action.

---

## MOVES

**FDA proposed what a surgical robot must show before market.** Draft guidance published 25 September "provides draft recommendations regarding non-clinical and clinical testing and premarket submission content for RASDs", Docket FDA-2026-N-9505, comments closing 24 November 2026. It "does not establish any rights for any person and is not binding on FDA or the public". ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/25/2026-19704/robotically-assisted-surgical-devices-premarket-submissions-draft-guidance-for-industry-and-food-and)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

`buried`: RASDs are defined as "teleoperated, software-controlled systems", so a learned autonomous policy sits outside this document.

**An outside audit reversed who won.** Seven simulated manipulation benchmarks, including RoboTwin, LIBERO-Plus and VLABench, were checked against their own intent: "we identify 22 bugs of these types and 4 design limitations". Fixing them "can reverse method rankings, moving the baseline from last to first on one task", and on another the baseline "moves from 21 percentage points behind an accelerated method to 5 points ahead". ([arXiv 2609.37771](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37771)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`assurance-seam` · **supports** · published scores were wrong by more than the effect being claimed, and a party auditing the harness rather than running it is what found that. Bound: the auditors released fixes, not a verdict.

**Telemetry matched internal access, again.** Auditing latent-space failure monitors on two autonomous-driving tasks, a monitor using only LaneSegNet's prediction outputs reaches AUROC 0.825, and for VAD ego state, driving command and predicted trajectory reach 0.924. "Adding latent features to either baseline yields no statistically resolved improvement." ([arXiv 2609.30557](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30557)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`assurance-seam` · **weakens** · if observable inputs and outputs predict failure as well as privileged internal access, the examiner's claim to need access the operator must grant weakens. Bound: failure prediction is not regression detection.

---

Recital 27 of the Regulation states that "in the machinery sector, approximately 98 % of companies are small or medium sized enterprises (SMEs)" and that "it is important that notified bodies consider adapting the fees for conformity assessment and reducing them proportionately to the specific interests and needs of SMEs". Article 25(5) makes it an obligation rather than an aspiration: "Notified bodies shall take into account the specific interests and needs of small and medium sized enterprises when setting the fees for conformity assessment" ([CELEX 32023R1230](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1230)). So the buyer base is overwhelmingly small, and pricing is unregulated but carries a statutory duty to flex downward for most of the market.

Next: the four-house TIC market spread, then §1 the constraint.

Recorded taps on a real arm have now been replayed under an injected model error, which the 18 September capture said would kill the surviving thesis outright: does that fire the kill test, or do proprioceptive probes fall short of contact under a changed action, in which case the thesis needs restating in those words?

# Thursday 1 October 2026

Window 30 September to 1 October. 1,520 considered, 4 included, 1 number in DIFFS.

---

## THE ONE THING

The EU corrected the sentence deciding whether an AI system is a safety component. A corrigendum to Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, published 29 September, replaces one word in new AI Act Article 6(1b)'s German text: "Unbeschadet des Absatzes 1a" becomes "Ungeachtet des Absatzes 1a". The English reads "Notwithstanding paragraph 1a, AI systems the failure or malfunctioning of which would endanger health and safety shall qualify as safety components." The published German used "Unbeschadet" there and eleven times elsewhere, and "Ungeachtet" nowhere, so for 67 days the clause overriding the carve-out was worded like one preserving it. ([corrigendum](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/cellar/1d32c7c2-bb9e-11f1-81de-01aa75ed71a1.0001), [English text](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1744)) · *geo · primary-filing · two-source*

`buried`: Art. 6(1a), new to the board, excludes AI systems "solely used for non-safety related aspects of user assistance, performance optimisation, service efficiency, automation or convenience or quality control".

---

## MOVES

**OpenAI named a lab and closed a replay path.** Extraction of protected reasoning began 1 July and spiked to 16,000 requests from over 4,000 users on 24 and 25 July, inside a cluster of more than 15,000 users, disrupted by 28 July. OpenAI attributes "a core cluster of the activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI", and "closed a pathway that allowed someone who already possessed another user's encrypted reasoning to replay it and recover its contents". ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/disrupting-a-coordinated-model-distillation-campaign/)) · *geo · primary-company · single-source*

`assurance-seam` · **weakens** · "Systems that support portable or replayable reasoning artifacts may face related risks" gives operators a security reason to foreclose the replay the thesis needs.

**A self-issued certificate was valid and wrong in every instance.** Corrupting only the committed graph of a causal action verifier takes it from zero false executions to 15.3%; reversing one arrowhead gives 48.9% and no correct ones. "Every one of these actions carries an internally valid certificate." An attestation step against a bounded randomised sample caught both attacks, at 2 false alarms in 555 executions. ([arXiv 2609.40027](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40027)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`assurance-seam` · **supports** · and prices the seat: "Recovering safety costs 127 experiments per 1,050 actions; recovering the lost value costs 614 more."

**A model-replacement gate ran on a real quadruped's contact data.** On a Unitree Go2, pre-contact images map to five proprioceptive indicators including planar foot slip and touchdown loading rate. "Candidate models replace the deployed predictor only when they improve performance on recent held-out data while keeping degradation on historical held-out data within a prescribed tolerance." Over three unseen terrains the gate cut final anchor NLL degradation 23.1%. ([arXiv 2609.39755](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39755)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`assurance-seam, surviving form` · **weakens** · an operator gated its own update against its own historical contact data on hardware, no third party, no throughput surrendered. Bound, and where the thesis stands: stored data was re-scored, the prior policy never re-executed.

---

## DIFFS

`Reg (EU) 2026/1744, German Art. 6(1b): was "Unbeschadet" (24 Jul) -> now "Ungeachtet"` [CELLAR corrigendum]

`AI Act safety-component carve-out: none tracked -> Art. 6(1a) names six excluded uses` [CELEX 32026R1744]

`Colocation liquid cooling, first price tracked: $28,751.20/mo at ~28.75 kVA (1yr) -> $23,000.96 (3yr); install $56,312.16; customer cabinet $2,500, no monthly` [[Nasdaq ISE, 2026-09-30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/09/30/2026-19949.txt)]

`Board: eu-machinery-2027 gains the Art. 6(1a)/(1b) qualification test` [data/library.js]

---

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

Serialising `reports/terrain-map.md` §1, the money.

Market size, and the spread is again the finding rather than the number. Four research houses size the 2026 testing, inspection and certification market at USD 254.41 billion ([MarketsandMarkets](https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/Market-Reports/testing-inspection-certification-market-5352498.html)), USD 275.39 billion ([Astute Analytica](https://www.astuteanalytica.com/industry-report/testing-inspection-certification-tic-market)), USD 280.2 billion, and USD 320.55 billion ([Business Research Insights](https://www.businessresearchinsights.com/market-reports/testing-inspection-and-certification-tic-market-117693)). A 26% spread on a market this mature means the houses disagree about what counts as in scope, so no single figure here should be quoted as the market size. Asia Pacific is put at roughly 38% of it in 2026.

Next: §1 the constraint, Article 30(8).

---

## ONE QUESTION

Art. 6(1a) excludes an AI system solely used for quality control from being a safety component: does that put visual inspection and weld-quality policies, where most paying deployments sit, outside the 2027 notified-body obligation, yes or no?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: about 1,520 records from 5 collectors (F1 Capital Ledger, F3 Policy Diff, F4 Frontier Claims, F5 Thesis Sentry, F6 Voices). Included: 4 as prose items, plus one number carried in DIFFS only. Dropped as duplicate: 2. Dropped as off-axis, below floor or out of window: the remainder.

The second was Approval Laundering (arXiv 2609.38983), which instruments Claude Code's PreToolUse mediation point across six failure modes at N=19-20 runs each with inter-rater kappa=1.0 and reports that the assumption "that the action A a human approves is the same action A' the harness executes" fails "systematically and reproducibly"; a keyed Approval Token tested by paired replay of 118 runs "fully eliminates Delegation laundering" and Temporal laundering at p<10^-5 "but by design leaves Scope laundering unaffected". It supports `assurance-seam`, because the gap between authorised and executed was found by instrumenting the mediation point rather than by reading the harness's own report, and because the remedy provably does not close all of it. Bound: coding agents rather than robot policies, and the authors built both the taxonomy and the token. It was cut rather than one of the three kept because it changes no tracked number, creates no date and names no new actor, which is the charter's ranking order. On the structural claim it is the strongest supporting item in the window, and cutting it leaves MOVES carrying one supporting and two weakening items, so the balance of this brief's MOVES understates the supporting side. The Directive is not on the instrument watchlist and the item changes no tracked number. One is reported above. No record in any listing carries a 1 October publication date, so the arXiv half of today's window is one day wide, not two. 420 matched the thesis filter and 12 were read in full. Eight targeted full-text searches, on over-the-air updates, third-party conformity assessment, non-regression, contact dynamics replay, notified body, robot policy regression testing, independent evaluators and AI Act safety components, returned no additional in-window record. Affiliations are not carried on arXiv records and were not separately retrieved, so no author affiliation is claimed above. Read and cut besides Approval Laundering: `2609.39717` Runtime Assurance Contracts, where "aggregate performance cannot authorize action" and a published score rule admits 80 of 100 block-required injections, cut because its cases are synthetic; `2609.38956`, an exact-null audit showing the apparent gain from privileged internal routing signals falls from 27.5% (528/1,920) to zero detections once checkpoints are selected on validation log loss, which pushes the 30 September outputs-versus-latent finding further and was cut only for space; `2609.40306` DynaHarness, where "Paired regression checks govern admission or rejection" of a self-evolving robot agent's revisions, 75.2% against 17.5% for the frozen policy on 800 new initial states, in simulation; `2609.39235`, where a world model's planning limit "persists under perfect prediction", success falling from 92% to 41%, which bears on `twin-certification`; `2609.39182` MEND, label-free detection of latent hallucination in world models at AUROC up to 0.80; `2609.37315`, an executable-contract audit confirming seven tool defects across four agent benchmarks; and `2609.39537`, where LLM-assisted classification of EU AI Act compliance evidence reaches kappa 0.045 in the employment domain, which cuts against the Governance-as-Code automation argument already on the board.

# Friday 2 October 2026

Window 1 to 2 October. 900 considered, 4 included, 1 in DIFFS only.

---

## THE ONE THING

Anthropic put $100 million behind a credential it grades itself. Claude Frontier Academy, launched 2 October, "aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027", first cohorts from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley and Novo Nordisk. It "follows the medical model": engineers "are assessed on their work before they earn the credential", finish "with a graded practical on a new scenario" for a Resident Engineer badge, then a 12-week residency and a second assessment for the FDE badge, first expected early 2027. ([Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-frontier-academy)) · *money · primary-company · single-source*

`bears_on` the constraint reading: terrain-map §1 prices capacity as assessor headcount under Article 30(8). Here the vendor pays, grades and badges, at $10,000 a head on this system's arithmetic.

---

## MOVES

**The executive branch stopped saying "artificial intelligence".** Executive Order 14434, signed 29 September, published 2 October, orders that the executive branch "shall use the terms 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence' and 'AI' and will not acknowledge the usage of" the old terms. By 28 November 2026 the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology must propose legislative language including "an assessment of whether, and to what extent" the new definition "should modify, expand upon, or otherwise supersede the existing statutory definition". ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/02/2026-20321/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

`buried`: none. SI means AI as defined at 15 U.S.C. 9401(3) until superseded.

**The Commission cited 19 harmonised standards and gave 18 months to switch.** Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2211, published 2 October, adds 19 references under the Pressure Equipment Directive and deletes 18 superseded rows, deferring that deletion to 2 April 2028 "In order to give manufacturers sufficient time to adapt their products to the revised versions of harmonised standards". EN 12953-6:2024 is cited with a restriction because it "contains technical shortcomings". ([CELEX 32026D2211](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026D2211)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

**A 99 percent release gate needs 5,182 tests once its tests correlate.** Treating the gate as a design problem: "In one configuration, a 99 percent target needs 8 independent tests, but 74 tests at a latent correlation of 0.3 and 5,182 at 0.5, where the gate keeps fewer than one good model in ten." Under pass-all gating "the share of good models kept tends to zero as the suite grows". ([arXiv 2610.00993](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00993)) · *thesis · primary-author · single-source*

`assurance-seam` · **supports** · it makes "it passed the suite" an unsupported claim and puts the competence in gate design. Bound: a latent-factor model, no policies, published free.

---

## DIFFS

`AI Act Art. 57 sandboxes: was 2026-08-02 -> now 2027-08-02, 194 days after the Machinery date` [[CELEX 32026R1744 Art. 1(22)(a)](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1744)]

`Board: eu-machinery-2027 gains the 2027-08-02 sandbox date` [data/library.js]

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

Serialising `reports/terrain-map.md` §1, the constraint.

Accredited competence, a people constraint rather than a capital one. The binding text is Article 30(8): "The remuneration of the top-level management and the personnel responsible for carrying out the conformity assessment tasks shall not depend on the number of conformity assessments carried out or on the results of those assessments." That single sentence removes the two levers a normal services business would use to scale, paying assessors on volume and paying them on outcome. Growth therefore comes only from hiring and accrediting more assessors, which is slow. Per the register, that headcount sits in few institutions: 7 of the 41 bodies are DGUV Test units of one German body ([CELEX 32023R1230](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1230)).

Next: the Article 30(9) and 30(10) paragraph, then §1 the live disagreement.

The EU's own supervised pre-market testing venues need not be operational until 2 August 2027, 194 days after the Machinery obligation bites: is the 20 January 2027 date therefore unenforceable in practice, yes or no?

Out of window and named so a later run reads rather than rediscovers them: "Partnering with Accenture on embedded evaluation", 18 September, and "Introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program", 17 September, both of which bear directly on the embedded-evaluator evidence the board already holds from 12 September. # Monday 5 October 2026

Window 2 to 5 October. 674 considered, 3 included, 4 in DIFFS.

---

## THE ONE THING

OpenAI shipped text watermarking into the EU and kept the detector. Published today: API watermarking is opt-in and "will remain off by default in the API"; an invisible watermark reaches ChatGPT and Codex output "in the European Union" only; detector access opens to "approved researchers and expert organizations", and "we are not making it publicly available at launch". AI Act Article 50(2) has required since 2 August 2026 that outputs be "marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated", with solutions "robust and reliable as far as this is technically feasible". OpenAI published the robustness figures itself: replacing 25% of words with synonyms cut detection to 17%. ([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/eu-text-provenance/), [CELEX 32024R1689](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1689)) · *geo · primary-company and primary-filing · two-source*

`bears_on` the foreclosure argument of 1 October: the incentive is to ration the checking, not the mark.

---

## MOVES

**A regulator priced a credential at $100 and required that anyone can check it.** Five SEC notices today propose designating the CPA licence, CFA charter, CFP certification and Series 79, 86 and 87 licences as qualifying for accredited investor status, plus "an accredited investor exam ... to be developed by" FINRA. The fourth attribute in Rule 501(a)(10) is that holding it "is either made publicly available by the relevant self-regulatory organization ... or is otherwise independently verifiable". Anticipated fee $100, about 75 questions, valid ten years. ([Federal Register](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/05/2026-20310/potential-designation-of-passage-of-an-accredited-investor-exam-to-be-developed-by-finra-as)) · *money · primary-filing · single-source*

`bears_on` the credentialed-competence line: Anthropic's badge of 2 October is "by nomination" at $10,000 a head, with no register.

**A world model was forked exactly and still did not register its own action.** Exact simulator-state forks in a deformable-physics testbed. "Changed commands alter particle motion, yet 41.5% of one-step raster pairs are identical." Across 579 high-visibility counterfactuals the median predictor-to-target response is 0.0051 and 0.0217 on two seeds, while a matched state perturbation moves the predictor 190x and 53x more, "isolating action-path under-use". "Neither error nor rank alone certifies physical state." ([arXiv 2610.02860](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02860)) · *new · primary-research · self-reported*

`bears_on` the decision carried since 18 September: where the counterfactual is free, the changed action is often invisible in the observation. A second obstacle behind non-replayability.

**A robot safety monitor was audited against itself and missed every targeted case.** RoboGuard's verdict on a surface plan was compared with its verdict on a graph-refined trace under one LTL specification. "In the controlled evaluation, all 12 targeted abstraction cases exhibit the predicted surface-versus-refined discrepancy while all 16 controls behave as expected." Five action-abstraction families, plus 14 end-to-end cases with SPINE generating plans. ([arXiv 2610.02662](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02662)) · *new · primary-research · self-reported*

---

## DIFFS

`Notified bodies: 41 under Reg 2023/1230, 153 under Dir 2006/42/EC, unchanged; 26.8%, 107 days to application` [[register](https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/single-market-compliance-space/#/notified-bodies/notified-body-list)]

`Accredited-investor credentials: was 3 since 2020-08-26 -> now 3 plus 5 under notice, comments close 12-04` [SEC, Release 33-11445]

`Credential price: $10,000 vendor-graded (Anthropic, 10-02) against $100 SRO-examined and publicly verifiable (FINRA)` [both releases]

`EIA Dir 2011/92/EU Annex II 10(b), Danish: "Anlægsarbejder i byzoner" -> "Byudviklingsprojekter", 5,364 days on` [[ELI](http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/92/corrigendum/2026-10-05/oj)]

`ISO/CD 25785-1: stage 30.60 unchanged, fourth consecutive reading` [[ISO](https://www.iso.org/standard/91469.html)]

`AI Act Art. 50(2) applied 2026-08-02 -> first frontier-lab text watermark 64 days later` [own arithmetic]

`Board: assurance-seam dek revised, "that distinction is now the whole thesis" no longer holds` [data/library.js]

---

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

Serialising `reports/terrain-map.md` §1, the constraint, paragraph two.

Two further requirements shape the cost base. Article 30(9) requires liability insurance "unless liability is assumed by the Member State in accordance with national law". Article 30(10) imposes professional secrecy over everything learned during an assessment, which is what makes a notified body usable by competitors simultaneously and is therefore an asset, not a cost ([CELEX 32023R1230](http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32023R1230)).

Next: §1 the live disagreement.

---

## ONE QUESTION

Article 50(2) requires an output to be "detectable as artificially generated" without saying by whom, and on the day a provider shipped a mark whose detector it rations, a US regulator wrote independent verifiability into what makes a credential count: is a disclosure obligation whose only verifier is the discloser satisfied, yes or no?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: about 674 records from 5 collectors. 384 arXiv records submitted 2 to 5 October in cs.RO, cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.SE and cs.CY, 106 Federal Register documents, 19 EU sector-3 acts by OJ publication date (57 across all sectors), 150 Form D filings of 2 October, 15 lab and voices page items. # Monday 12 October 2026

Window 10 to 12 October, plus arXiv for 9 October. 421 considered, 4 included,
6 DIFFS.

---

## THE ONE THING

A NeurIPS 2026 paper shows a capability audit can be defeated with a proof.
Draguns, Motwani, Douglas and Schroeder de Witt embed encrypted neural networks
inside host model weights, decrypting and executing them "only upon receiving a
secret trigger". The hidden circuits "remain provably hard to elicit and
interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model
weights". Fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search
and latent adversarial training all failed to elicit them on a chemical reaction
task, "a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities". The stated result: "a limit of
elicitation-based capability audits".
([arXiv 2610.13928](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13928)) · *thesis · paper, NeurIPS 2026 · single-source*

`bears_on` assurance-seam, which needs a party able to state with validity what
a learned system does. It bounds what weight access buys.

---

## MOVES

**A monitor's accuracy was separated from its worth.** CSIRO's RESCUE restores simulator and policy states at execution checkpoints and compares alternative actions across 128,340 counterfactual branches, on OpenVLA-OFT and π0.5 over LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Plus. "Favourable detection scores do not establish lower intervention cost." Under a stop-and-reset model, "even an idealised detector can afford only a 2.0-3.3% false-alarm rate before unnecessary resets outweigh the savings from stopping failures early". ([arXiv 2610.13516](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13516)) · *thesis · paper · single-source*

**A replay bench reached physical hardware.** JitterVLA "replays identical commands and arrival traces through alternative controllers", across hand trajectories from 20 people, three open VLA pipelines at 838 episodes, and a physical UR3. Interpolation lowered modeled p99 jerk 83%, from 615 to 106 m/s^3, at 200 ms delay and a 2.0 cm tracking cost. On the UR3 it lowered accelerometer-derived jerk 3.0 to 14.0%. What is replayed is the command stream, not contact under a changed action. ([arXiv 2610.13628](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13628)) · *thesis · paper · single-source*

**A paper wrote down what a governance answer must contain to be checkable.** Rosenbacke et al. hold that "a checkable answer needs a named person, a date, a number, and a stop that has been used or tested", and define control as someone who "can detect a serious problem, challenge the decision, stop the system and reverse it, and who has something to lose by not doing so". ([arXiv 2610.13340](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13340)) · *thesis · paper, no number · single-source*

---

## DIFFS

`assurance-seam kill test: was 2 labs committed, no counterparty, no figure (2026-09-12) -> now Accenture named, "at least $1 billion" each over five years, paid by Anthropic. Out of window, 2026-09-18` [[Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/accenture-embedded-evaluation)]

`corrigendum pattern: was 4 consecutive single-language (2026-10-05) -> now broken, EDIP Reg (EU) 2025/2643 corrected in all languages at 287 days` [[ELI](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/2643/corrigendum/2026-10-12/oj)]

`Board: assurance-seam card gains the elicitation limit, the monitor ceiling and the Accenture figure` [data/library.js]

---

## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

`reports/terrain-map.md` §1, the recent history, second paragraph. Completes it.

"The designation mechanics, since the two-step structure is what causes the
delay: under Article 33(2) the application goes to the notifying authority with
an accreditation certificate from a national accreditation body 'where one
exists', or under Article 33(3) with full documentary evidence if not. Then
under Article 34(5) the body 'may perform the activities of a notified body only
where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States
within two weeks of the validation of the notification where it includes an
accreditation certificate, or within two months of the notification where it
includes documentary evidence'. So the final objection window is two weeks with
accreditation and two months without, which means accreditation is the long pole
and the notification step is fast."

Next: §1 "what is missing from this section".

---

## ONE QUESTION

If a capability can be hidden in weights so that an auditor holding those
weights provably cannot elicit it, is the sellable asset access during training
rather than method, yes or no?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: 421 records from 5 collectors. 347 unique arXiv records across cs.RO, cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.SE and cs.CY, all dated 9 October; 74 EU documents by OJ publication date across 10 to 12 October; 0 Federal Register documents; 0 Form D filings; 5 voices pages; 3 frontier-lab publication feeds. Included: 3 as prose items plus the lead. 5 carried in DIFFS. Dropped as off-axis, out of window or duplicate: the remainder.

THE WINDOW IS SPLIT, and the split is deliberate rather than a convenience. Today is Monday, so the charter window is 72 hours, 9 to 12 October. The 11 October brief already collected the Federal Register, EU and Form D records of 8 and 9 October, so for those three sources this run covers 10 to 12 October only, to avoid repeating items. That brief's provenance also recorded that every one of its 495 arXiv records carried a submission date of 8 October, that 9 and 10 October had not propagated to the API index, and that a later run should expect them late. 9 October has now appeared and is collected here. 10 and 11 October are a weekend and 12 October is Columbus Day, so three of the four document sources have no publication day at all in the 10 to 12 October part of the window. This is a quiet window by the calendar, not by judgement.

THREE SOURCES ARE STRUCTURALLY EMPTY, each verified rather than assumed. The Federal Register daily facet endpoint returns a count of 0 for 10, 11 and 12 October, against 133 on 8 October and 89 on 9 October, which reconciles exactly with the 222 the last run reported, and 103 documents are already filed for 13 October. The EDGAR daily-index directory for 2026 QTR4 ends at form.20261009.idx, so there is no filing day in window and F1 Capital Ledger had no primary source; form.20261012.idx returns a 212-byte error body rather than an index. One secondary search for rounds announced 10 to 12 October returned aggregator pages only and nothing dated in window, and the charter forbids a secondary or social source as the sole basis for a funding number, so F1's output is: no qualifying items in window.

F6 Voices: zero items, the expected output and the eighth consecutive one. All four venues read over HTTP with a desktop User-Agent and no browser pane. darioamodei.com returned exactly four `/post/` and two `/essay/` hrefs, matching the stored list. Paul Graham's top six titles read identically to the stored list and in the stored order, a seventh consecutive run for the stored-title diff. karpathy.bearblog.dev returned HTTP 200, newest still Sequoia Ascent 2026 of 30 April; karpathy.github.io unchanged at 12 February 2026. No voice changed position.

F3 Policy Diff. `tools/eurlex.mjs since 2026-10-10 --to 2026-10-12 --sector all` listed 74 documents, all carrying the OJ date of 12 October; 10 and 11 October carry none. One is a corrigendum and it is promoted to DIFFS. The remainder are 10 CFSP and sanctions implementing acts, 3 merger and state-aid notices, 6 sanctions notices, and roughly 40 Court of Justice judgments and preliminary-ruling requests. Checked by name and dropped: Case C-733/26 Glass Machinery Reconditioners, which despite the party name asks whether the actio judicati limitation period falls inside "procedure for the enforcement of judgments" under Brussels Ibis Article 41(1) and has nothing to do with machinery safety. Also checked and dropped: Case T-357/24 Opera Norway v Commission and Case C-909/26 P, Meta's appeal, neither of which creates an obligation on this board's axes. No watchlist instrument moved. The notified-body register was NOT re-read: it was read on 11 October at 41 under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, the intervening days are a weekend and a federal holiday, and a seventh consecutive reading of 41 would be a manufactured DIFF. The count of days to 20 January 2027 stands at 100 on this system's arithmetic. standards.cencenelec.eu was not retried and prEN 50742 remains dormant; iso.org was not re-read.

THE CORRIGENDUM, and why it is a DIFF rather than a MOVE. Regulation (EU) 2025/2643 is the EDIP Regulation, establishing the European Defence Industry Programme, and it is not on the watchlist. The correction is carried because it breaks the cross-instrument pattern this board stated once on 5 October so that later runs would stop rediscovering it: four consecutive corrigenda, each altering an operative word in exactly one language version. This one was issued in all language versions at once, 287 days after the OJ of 29 December 2025, and it corrects an internal cross-reference rather than a word of substance. Retrieved by the SPARQL expression-URI route, since `eurlex.mjs get` returns "not found" for an R(01) suffix, which is the standing note holding for a third run.

F4 Frontier Claims. Lab publication pages produced nothing dated in window. Anthropic's newest is 8 October, genesis-mission-commitment; OpenAI's newest is 9 October; DeepMind's newest is 6 October. Each date was read from the page's own datePublished or pubDate field rather than inferred from listing order. TWO RETRIEVAL FIXES, both found today and neither previously recorded. openai.com/news returns HTTP 403 to an HTTP client, while openai.com/news/rss.xml returns 200 with 1,287 dated items, which makes the 403 a non-issue rather than a browser-pane escalation. deepmind.google/discover/blog is a 301 to deepmind.google/blog, whose rss.xml returns a gzip body that must be fetched with `curl --compressed` or it reads as binary and every date regex silently returns nothing, which is the same silent-failure shape as the arXiv http-versus-https trap recorded on 6 October. Read and cut for space: arXiv 2610.13479, a laptop-based agentic framework in which a local language model generates edge-case scenarios and "a second, independent LM critiques each scenario using domain specific criteria", producing what the authors call "traceable evidence for the safety assurance case". It carries no number, which is why it was cut, and its direction is weakening, because the independent critic is a second instance of the same class of system as the thing under test. Also cut from the third MOVES item for the word cap, and recorded here because it is the board-relevant claim in that paper: its stated ordering is "Publication is the first step and one laboratory can take it alone; the contract, the independent body and the law come after", which puts the independent body third rather than first.

F5 Thesis Sentry. Three items, and the weakening side is the better evidenced again. Weakening assurance-seam, and it is the day's strongest: arXiv 2610.13928 bounds what an auditor can establish from model weights alone, under cryptographic assumptions and against four named elicitation methods, which cuts at the thesis claim that a neutral party can state with validity what a learned system does. The bound on that reading, and it matters: the construction is a backdoor deliberately inserted by whoever trained the model, so it bounds the audit of an adversarial developer and says nothing about an honest developer's unintended capability. Weakening, at equal prominence: RESCUE puts a ceiling of 2.0 to 3.3% on the false-alarm rate an idealised detector can carry before it costs more than it saves, which prices the intervention rather than the measurement, and finds that detection score does not establish intervention value. Changes-the-clock: the Accenture correction recorded below. Supporting, and this is the honest count: nothing in window.

THE LEDGER CORRECTION, which is the part of this run that matters most and which no collector found in window. The assurance-seam kill test asks whether any buyer pays for third-party attestation rather than open-sourcing the tool or using its own telemetry. This board has carried "Anthropic and OpenAI both committing to embedded third-party evaluators 2026-09-12" as evidence for, with no counterparty and no figure. Anthropic named both on 18 September, in a post absent from every file in reports/, data/ and logs/: the partner is Accenture, the work is "led by Faculty, Accenture's specialist AI business", it covers "evaluating and red-teaming models, conducting alignment assessments, and testing model safeguards", and "Anthropic and Accenture each expect to invest at least $1 billion in building capacity in this area over the next five years". The funding structure is the finding rather than the figure: "Long-term, we think funding should come from pooled or government sources", but as neither exists today, "Anthropic will fund Accenture's work directly", and the post states "There are, as yet, no standards for what information embedded evaluators should have access to, or how they should report what they find". That is a buyer paying, and it is also the audited party paying the auditor with no standard governing the report. The post is dated 18 September and is therefore outside this window, so it is carried in DIFFS as a correction with its date stated rather than promoted to MOVES, because date-laundering a 24-day-old post into today's items is the failure the dateline rule exists to prevent. The miss is recorded in knowledge-state so that no later run rediscovers it.

# Wednesday 14 October 2026

Window 13 to 14 October. 294 considered, 4 included, 5 DIFFS.

---

## THE ONE THING

The EU cited its first harmonised standard under the AI Act. Commission
Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274, published 14 October and in force that
day, publishes the reference of EN 18286:2026, "Artificial intelligence –
Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes". It is the only entry in
the Annex and answers point 9 of the 2025 standardisation request, on "quality
management systems for providers of AI systems, including post-market
monitoring processes". No earlier citation exists in 5,000 sector-3 documents
since the AI Act was published. Machinery Article 20(10) carries it
across: AI Act harmonised standards confer presumption of conformity under the
Machinery Regulation until machinery ones exist. The register still returns
zero notified bodies under the AI Act.
([OJ](http://data.europa.eu/eli/dec_impl/2026/2274/oj)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

---

## MOVES

**Two bodies were notified under the Machinery Regulation, both SGS.** The register, read 14 October, returns 43 active under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, against 41 on six readings from 22 September to 11 October. The complete 43-name capture diffs cleanly against the 41 stored on 30 September: NB 1637 SGS-TÜV Saar GmbH, Germany, and NB 1179 SGS – Statutory Services Belgium. Belgium enters the list, and SGS now holds three. Ratio 28.1% against 153, 98 days out. ([register](https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/single-market-compliance-space/notified-bodies/notified-body-list?filter=notificationStatusId:1,legislationId:162400)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

**A third party asked whether a simulation twin is good enough to rank policies, and could not answer.** YUBI-Real2Sim, 13 October, builds scenes with 3D Gaussian Splatting and tests whether real-to-sim evaluation preserves policy ordering, "reproducing the observed real-world policy ordering in eight of nine scene-task comparisons" across two bimanual platforms, three scenes and three tasks. On whether reconstruction-quality scores predict that: "These results do not yet establish a generally reliable scene-acceptance rule." ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17521)) · *thesis · primary-filing · single-source*

**The ITC opened an exclusion proceeding over AI datacenter power delivery.** Investigation 337-TA-1526, instituted 9 October on Vicor Corporation's complaint, reaches "vertical power delivery systems and components thereof, used in data center server, artificial intelligence and cloud computing systems, to power artificial intelligence (`AI') accelerators, tensor processing units (`TPU'), graphical processing units (`GPU') and central processing units (`CPU')". Twenty respondents, among them Foxconn, Quanta, Delta, Infineon and Flex. Vicor requests "a limited exclusion order and cease and desist orders". ([FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/14/2026-20993/certain-vertical-power-delivery-systems-components-thereof-and-computing-systems-containing-the-same)) · *geo · primary-filing · single-source*
