## FROM THE STOCK SIDE

`reports/terrain-map.md` §1, what is missing, second paragraph. It completes §1.

"Still not found: any published fee schedule or day rate for a machinery
conformity assessment, the utilisation rate or revenue per assessor of a
notified body, and the duration of the accreditation step rather than the
notification step. Bureau Veritas is used above as the margin reference because
it publishes; TÜV SÜD, TÜV Rheinland and DEKRA are structured such that
comparable segment margins were not located. No primary document on what a
notified body charges has been read, which was the specific gap this section
was written to close and which it has only partly closed."

§1 is exhausted. The marker says §2 is a skeleton to omit; read today it has
two prose paragraphs carrying figures, so the next run has a choice.

---

## ONE QUESTION

A standard conferring presumption of conformity now exists under the AI Act
and reaches machinery through Article 20(10), while nobody is notified to
assess against it: is a cited standard with no assessor enough to make
20 January 2027 dischargeable?

---

## PROVENANCE

Considered: 294 records from 5 collectors. 49 EU documents by OJ publication date of 13 and 14 October in sector 3, 229 Federal Register documents of 13 and 14 October, 237 Form D filings in the EDGAR index of 13 October reduced to 50 at or above the $10M floor, 57 arXiv cs.RO submissions of 13 October matching the evaluation and safety filter, 5 voices pages, 3 frontier-lab feeds. Counted once where a document appears in two collectors. Included: 3 as prose items plus the lead. 5 carried in DIFFS. Dropped as duplicate: 1. Dropped as off-axis, out of window or below floor: the remainder.

WORD CAP. The first draft ran to 891 words excluding this block against a ceiling of 700, and five passes brought it to 695. A word changed inside a verbatim quoted sentence during the fourth pass was caught and restored on the fifth. Two cuts are judgements and not tidying, and both are named. A fourth MOVES item, the Anthropic MOU with Singapore, was cut to the paragraph below; it was chosen because it carries no figure and moves no date, which is the ranking rule, not because the counterparty matters less. Three DIFFS lines were also moved below rather than deleted, for the same reason.

WINDOW. Wednesday, so the last 24 hours, 13 to 14 October. The 13 October brief covered EU documents of 13 October, so one duplicate was expected and found: corrigendum `32026R0798R(02)` to the eIDAS implementing Regulation, OJ ref 2026/90863, is the same Slovak correction already reported yesterday and was dropped rather than re-reported.

THE LEAD'S NOVELTY WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSERTED. `node tools/eurlex.mjs since 2024-08-01 --to 2026-10-13 --match "harmonised standards for high-risk AI|support of Regulation \(EU\) 2024/1689"` returns "no match ... 5000 document(s) in window", so no earlier AI Act harmonised-standard citation exists in sector 3 across that period. The Machinery Article 20(10) text was grepped out of CELEX 32026R1744 and reads in full: "Until harmonised standards or common specifications are referenced or adopted pursuant to this Article as regards high-risk AI systems, high-risk AI systems within the scope of this Regulation which comply with the relevant harmonised standards referenced, or common specifications adopted pursuant to Articles 40 and, respectively, 41 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 shall be presumed to be in conformity with the essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex III to this Regulation as regards high-risk AI systems." Stated as a bound rather than smoothed over: EN 18286:2026 is a quality management system standard answering AI Act Article 17, so what it can discharge through Article 20(10) is narrow, and nothing read today says it covers the Annex III essential health and safety requirements that Machinery Annex I Part A item 5 routes through a notified body.

THE REGISTER MOVE IS A NAME DIFF AND NOT A COUNT GUESS, which matters because the 5 October reading produced an inconclusive name diff from pagination instability. This run captured 30 rows on page 1 and 13 on page 2 with no overlap, totalling 43 against a heading of "Search results (43)". All 41 names stored on 30 September are present, and the two additions are NB 1637 and NB 1179. The URL-filter method recorded on 11 October worked first time at `webgate.ec.europa.eu`; the `single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu` host in the stored note returns "Page not found", so the host is corrected in the state file. NEXT ON THAT ROW, not done: whether NB 1637 and NB 1179 also hold a Directive 2006/42/EC notification, which separates new capacity from an existing body adding a scope. Page 1 of the Directive filter shows neither, but that is 30 of 153 rows and proves nothing.

SOURCES UNREACHABLE OR PARTIAL. arXiv returned HTTP 429 "Rate exceeded" on four consecutive calls after the first three succeeded, including every `id_list` call, so abstracts were read off `arxiv.org/abs/` pages instead and the cs.RO sweep for 13 October is the 60-record keyword query rather than a full listing. openai.com/index/the-eus-next-chapter-in-ai-is-agentic, published 14 October, returned HTTP 403 with "Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue"; only its RSS title, category "Global Affairs" and description were read, and the description describes an adoption analysis rather than an instrument, so it was dropped rather than escalated to a browser pane. cftc.gov was not retried this run and CFTC Release 9286-26 remains unread, as it was on 13 October.

F1 Capital Ledger, operating on priority 1 for the first time in three runs. EDGAR is back: form.20261013.idx returns 200 and 93,706 bytes, while form.20261012.idx returns 403, consistent with the 12 October federal holiday, and form.20261014.idx returns 403 because the day is not closed. All 237 Form D filings were fetched and parsed; 50 report at least $10,000,000 offered or sold. No qualifying item in an allowed sector. The largest operating-company filing was CURADEL SURGICAL INNOVATIONS, INC., Bonita Springs, Florida, totalOfferingAmount 57,500,000 and totalAmountSold 49,844,295, first sale 2026-09-18, signed by John V. Frangioni, M.D., Ph.D., self-reported industry "Biotechnology". It was DROPPED on the sector test and not the floor: curadel.com redirects to curadelpharma.com, which describes "proprietary zwitterionic technology to deliver best-in-class outcomes for targeted alpha therapy (TAT)", so despite the name this is not surgical robotics, and no company release was located. This is the Metaview and Athanor precedent of 6 and 11 October. Recorded so a later run does not rediscover it.

RECORDED OUT OF WINDOW, NOT PROMOTED, and both are misses by earlier runs. Anthropic committed "$150 million over three years to the Genesis Mission, a federal initiative to accelerate scientific and technological discovery through AI", in a post of 8 October, with the funding going to "more than 15 agencies that are part of the mission, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health, and the National Science Foundation", announced at the White House OSTP "Science: A New Golden Age Summit". That post is absent from every file in reports/, data/ and logs/, so it sat unrecorded for six days, and the 11 October run recovered 8 to 10 October without finding it. The same post describes the Model Hardware Standard as "a shared specification for AI agents to safely operate lab instruments", where this board stored "physical devices". Separately and in window, Google DeepMind and Google Cloud are "providing up to 200 top European scientific researchers with direct access to our frontier models, together with $3 million in compute credits", via the EU RAISE initiative, posted 14 October. The two are the same instrument, in-kind compute to a state science programme, at $150m against $3m on the companies' own figures. The DeepMind item was not promoted because it moves no tracked line and the comparison depends on an out-of-window figure.

F4 Frontier Claims, three records carried here rather than in MOVES on the word cap. LIBERO-RIG (arXiv 2610.18843, 13 October) perturbs only robot hardware and setup while holding LIBERO tasks fixed, across eleven axes and five severity levels giving 210 conditions, nine vision-language-action models, 500 episodes per condition: "Pooled success falls from 0.932 to 0.767 at the middle severity and 0.509 at the highest severity", and "training on visual perturbations does not mitigate faults that leave camera images unchanged". RoboFQE (arXiv 2610.18699, 13 October) estimates a target policy's discounted return from offline trajectories with no rollouts and reports that it "preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors"; it carries no headline number in its abstract. WorldOracle (arXiv 2610.18826, 13 October) benchmarks seven action-conditioned world models "against paired real-world executions" on four dimensions, from a team including NVIDIA-affiliated authors, with datasets, code and leaderboard promised rather than released. No pushback observed in window on any of the three; all are self-reported and none is replicated.

F5 Thesis Sentry, two items. WEAKENING twin-certification at equal prominence with yesterday's lead, which weakened it the other way: on 13 October Google's Argon put the twin and its validity test in the same model, and on the same day YUBI-Real2Sim had an unrelated group test whether a reconstructed twin preserves policy ordering and report that quality scores do not reliably predict it, which is a validity claim that someone has to make and that the builder's own score does not supply. WEAKENING the surviving form of assurance-seam, whose claim is that the previous policy cannot be run counterfactually without surrendering throughput: RoboFQE estimates a policy's return from trajectories another policy generated, with no rollouts and no simulator. Confidence, and it is the same bound as every prior instance: the method is free on arXiv, the kill test is "show one buyer paying for paired non-regression testing", and nobody is paying. SUPPORTING assurance-seam on the mandate half: an AI Act standard conferring presumption of conformity now exists with zero bodies notified to assess against it, which is a mandate with no one authorised to discharge it, the same shape recorded on 11 October and now with the standard half filled in.

CARRIED HERE RATHER THAN IN DIFFS, on the word cap, and all three are state-file updates. First, the Anthropic MOU with Singapore's Ministry of Digital Development and Information, 14 October, is NEW to the watchlist: it covers "areas of cooperation in AI safety, security, and model evaluation" and plans "technical exchanges with Singapore's AI safety, security, and assurance institutions on model evaluation, testing standards, and incident response", with no figure, no obligation and no reporting standard stated, signed by Kai Fong Chng for the Ministry and Ben Mann for Anthropic on the sidelines of Singapore International Cyber Week. The post does not say, and its independence criterion covers equity and financial or operational dependence without disclosing either way. The tension stated in THE ONE THING and in ONE QUESTION is therefore between the published criterion and the Accenture funding arrangement this board already holds, "Anthropic will fund Accenture's work directly", recorded 12 October, and not between the criterion and METR. Also in the post and not promoted: Anthropic "signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators", which is a new instrument this board has never logged and which nothing was read about today; and the bank-supervision analogy it offers, "regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks".

tracking, and recovery assessment, even in models with strong outcome and
forward-progress scores".
([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26663))
· *thesis · paper · single-source*

market. The mechanism is that the thesis has always been argued against the
commons objection, that the field prices evaluation at zero, and the semiconductor
test market is a standing counterexample where testing is bought at scale. THE

silicon by a test-equipment vendor taking a supply-chain stake, not a third

existing leaderboards are gameable, and then releases the specifications, build

buyer. That is the commons argument arriving for an eighth time on this exact
line, and it arrives inside the paper that makes the thesis's case. WEAKENING

digital-twin pipeline against real Idealworks robots and found it transfers,
65.3% to 91.7% and within 8.3 points of the production stack. The kill test on

accepting vendor sim evidence unaudited, and neither happened, so this is a
weakening and not a firing: what moved is that the validity measurement was
produced by a third party and published free, which supports the claim that the
statement is a separate thing and weakens the claim that it is sellable. The
kill test on assurance-seam is still answered yes only by the Accenture
arrangement.

into a broad technology collaboration"; this brief does not say the two
companies are merging, and the 8-K describes a private placement of common
stock and nothing more. No valuation is inferred for FormFactor from the share
count and the consideration, and the implied per-share figure is not computed
here because the 8-K says "approximately". Modal's $1B annualized run rate is

providers and an agency burden estimate, not a count of accredited certifiers,
and it is placed beside the 43 notified bodies as a scale comparison and not as
an equivalence. HATCH reports no results and this brief does not say its method
works.

term; then the Modal, FMCSA and HATCH items were tightened. No source sentence
was cut and no figure was dropped.

file they came from with a whitespace-normalising matcher that captures the
closing punctuation and folds curly quotes, dashes and non-breaking spaces, per

source is excluded rather than silently dropped. Both fragments were checked
against the HTML entity form in the raw filing as well as the tag-stripped

for a `meta` attribute.

# 2026-10-23

Friday, window 21 to 23 October, 48 hours because no brief ran on 22 October.
648 records from 5 collectors, 5 included.

---

## THE ONE THING

A federal regulator published how little of the evidence it reads.
FDA's ASCA collection, renewed 23 October under OMB control number 0910-0889:
"FDA generally accepts determinations by ASCA-accredited testing laboratories
that a device conforms with an eligible standard unless FDA determines that a
particular conformity determination should not be accepted", and "does not
intend to review complete test reports from ASCA-accredited testing
laboratories ... except in certain circumstances". Labs accredit against
ISO/IEC 17025:2017. FDA sizes the scheme at 8 accreditation bodies, 150
testing laboratories and 880 test reports a year, and cuts expected new
accreditation applications "from 150 to 50 respondents".
([FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21712/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-for-office-of-management-and-budget-review))
· *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

---

## MOVES

**A second model vendor now approves who may resell its models.** OpenAI, 21
October, states its Usage Policies are "effective November 20, 2026" and
"build on that work by requiring services that provide direct access to our
models such as model routers or AI gateways to get our review and approval
before offering that access". Partners must "maintain safeguards consistent
with our own, investigate potential violations, and take appropriate action".
Anthropic's policy conditioning customer hardware takes effect 12 November, 8
days earlier. The vendor is sole approver and no register is published.
([OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/broad-access-through-consistent-standards/))
· *geo · primary-company · single-source*

**Five language versions of the DSA ran a statutory lookback backwards for
1,457 days.** Eleventh corrigendum, OJ ref 2026/90910, published 23 October,
seven languages at once, no English expression. German, Finnish, Croatian,
Lithuanian and Slovene Article 32(1) read the six-month window as running from
the moment a marketplace learned of illegality; English reads "within the six
months preceding". Hungarian Article 35(1) cited "a 33. cikk" where English
reads "pursuant to Article 34", the risk assessment an Article 37 auditor
audits.
([ELI](http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/corrigendum/2026-10-23/oj))
· *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

**HHS approves exactly two entities to certify Medical Review Officers.**
Notice of 23 October, effective that day, signed by Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.:
the American Association of Medical Review Officers and the Medical Review
Officer Certification Council. Under Section 13.2 of the Mandatory Guidelines
each applicant submits "their qualifications, a sample examination, and other
necessary supporting examination materials", and each "must resubmit their
qualifications for approval every 2 years".
([FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21671/hhs-approval-of-entities-that-certify-medical-review-officers))
· *geo · primary-filing · single-source*

**$63,499,913 went into RISC-V CPU cores.** AheadComputing, Inc., Beaverton,
Oregon, incorporated 2024. Form D accepted 22 October, isAmendment false:
totalOfferingAmount 79,999,913, totalAmountSold 63,499,913, totalRemaining
16,500,000, 8 investors, first sale 2026-10-08, Rule 506(b). Directors named
on the filing include Jim Keller and Greg Reichow; Deborah Marr is executive
officer and director. The company's site: it builds "high-performance, RISC-V
cores that Modern AI-driven workloads demand".
([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2035028/000203502826000002/primary_doc.xml))
· *money · primary-filing · single-source*

---

## DIFFS

`vendor policies conditioning third parties by contract: was 1, Anthropic effective 2026-11-12 (10-11) -> now 2, OpenAI effective 2026-11-20` [[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/broad-access-through-consistent-standards/)]

`vendor agreements with a state assurance institution: was 1, Anthropic and Singapore MDDI (10-14) -> now 2, OpenAI and Poland's NASK, "serving as the Polish Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute (AISI)"` [[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/openai-nask-ai-safety-security-partnership/)]

`CAISSI: named by a second vendor, Anthropic only (10-20) -> now OpenAI, which expands it "Center for Advancing Standards and Innovation" against the stored "Advancing Innovation and Standards"` [[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/openai-nask-ai-safety-security-partnership/)]

`accredited testing laboratories under a US scheme, first count: 150 labs, 8 accreditation bodies, 880 test reports a year` [[FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21712/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-for-office-of-management-and-budget-review)]

`Anthropic access arrangements: was 4 (10-14) -> now 5, an open call for life-sciences guest investigators at no cost to them` [[Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/open-call-guest-investigators-life-sciences)]

`first pre-registered robot-learning study on this board: arms and tests registered "before any p-value", authors "withdraw - rather than refute" their own underpowered claim` [[arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30478)]

`data/library.js: assurance-seam gains the ASCA size, the two MRO certifiers and the OpenAI reseller gate` [own edit]

---

## ONE QUESTION

FDA says it generally will not read the test reports an accredited laboratory
produces, and in the same notice cuts its expected new accreditation
applications from 150 to 50: is a regulator declining to re-examine the
evidence what makes an assurance seat worth money, or the signal that the
seats are already taken?

---

## PROVENANCE

date of 22 and 23 October, sector 3; 178 Federal Register documents of 22 and

covers 48 hours rather than the charter's Tuesday-to-Friday 24. The task did
not fire on 22 October and nothing in the system noticed, which is the second

F3, AND THE CORRIGENDUM RETRIEVAL ROUTE, which is new and should not be

`tools/eurlex.mjs get "32022R2065R(11)"` returns "not found", and so does a

`cdm:resource_legal_id_celex`, then fetch each numbered expression at
`resource/cellar/<uuid>.000N` with `Accept: application/xhtml+xml`. That
returned all seven language versions. The English base text was read with
`eurlex grep 32022R2065` to establish what each language should have said.
Off-axis EU hits of 22 and 23 October, named so a later run does not re-derive
them: Commission Decision (EU) 2026/2349 recognising critical raw material

F1, ONE QUALIFYING ITEM. Of the 132 Form D filers fetched, 68 reported an

recorded so a later run does not re-derive them: Town.com, Inc., San
Francisco, sold 104,364,967 of 115,174,986 with 13 investors, self-reported
Other Technology, what it sells not established at source; Boltz, PBC, Boston,

F4 AND THE LAB FEEDS. openai.com/index returns HTTP 403 to an HTTP client, as

with no description, so both OpenAI items were read in a browser pane per the

and donating-agent-skills-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation, both `datePublished`
2026-10-22, and christopher-stubbs-joins-long-term-benefit-trust of
2026-10-21. Two further posts absent from this board are out of window,
enterprise-frontier-safeguards of 2026-09-01 and
improving-alignment-security-efforts of 2026-08-31, and they are misses by
earlier runs rather than news. DeepMind's newest is 22 October on forest-type

`http://export.arxiv.org` returns an empty body with curl exit 0, the same

Novelty checked by `grep -ril` over reports/, data/ and logs/ rather than

F5 THESIS SENTRY, THREE ITEMS AGAINST A CEILING OF THREE, and two of the three

# 2026-10-26

Monday, 72-hour window from the newest file in reports/newsletter/, not the
calendar. 588 considered, 5 included.

## THE ONE THING

Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 today, CIK 2130357, accession
0001628280-26-067168, to list Class A stock on Nasdaq as "ANT". The $1bn
evaluator programme recorded here on 2026-10-12 comes out smaller under
securities liability: "we currently anticipate investing at least $1 billion
over the next five years to build external reviewer capacity with Accenture.
The terms of this arrangement have not been finalized and are subject to
change." No Accenture figure appears. It also discloses what no post did:
certain evaluator agreements "require us to defend and indemnify the
evaluator, without a cap on our liability, against certain third-party
claims."
[S-1](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026067168/anthropicpbc-sx1.htm)
· geo/thesis · primary-filing · two-source

## MOVES

**Treasury proposes to prohibit the development of any SI system, and says why
it dropped the threshold.** Proposed rule, 31 CFR part 851, 91 FR 67396,
comments close 2026-12-07. Prohibited technology would include "(h) Development
of any SI system", because "no single measure, benchmark, or threshold is
currently sufficient to distinguish advanced models." Part 850 graded AI by
training compute. Buried: Sec. 851.232(b) puts "industrial robots, bipedal or
humanoid robots, quadruped robots, other mobile robots, autonomous vehicles,
and unmanned systems" inside the definition.
[FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21786/outbound-investment-security-program-regulations)
· geo · primary-filing · single-source

**A second regulator writes down that it will not repeat another's review.**
NRC final rule, 91 FR 67195, effective 2026-11-25. New 10 CFR 50.43(f): an
application "may include consideration of relevant information gathered from a
utilization facility that has been previously authorized by the Department of
Energy or the Department of Defense and that has been tested and has
demonstrated the ability to function safely." The NRC "will not need to repeat
technical reviews previously performed by DOE or DOW". ASCA's shape in a second
agency.
[FR](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21801/nrc-reviews-of-reactor-designs-previously-authorized-by-us-department-of-energy-or-department-of-war)
· geo · primary-filing · single-source

**$238,959,659 went into satellite positioning for machines.** Xona Space
Systems Inc., Burlingame. Form D in the 2026-10-23 EDGAR index, isAmendment
false: totalOfferingAmount 253,459,641, totalAmountSold 238,959,659, 28
investors, first sale 2026-10-08, exemption 06b. Its own site: "the navigation
infrastructure company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any
device, anywhere on Earth." No valuation or lead named.
[Form D](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920779/000110465926118524/primary_doc.xml)
· money · primary-filing · two-source

**Two papers the same day put the failure detector on opposite sides of the
wall.** CLAIM, arXiv 2610.32742 (AWARE, 23 October): anomaly detection "using
only external camera monitoring", written because "strict security protocols
may prohibit access altogether", at "a 26% improvement in anomaly
classification over our strongest baseline" over 240 real crane trajectories.
COUNTER, arXiv 2610.32208, same day: sparse autoencoder features of OpenVLA's
own activations "predict task failure before the robot reaches an
unrecoverable state". Second verifier-inside-the-policy after VeriVLA.
[2610.32742](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32742) ·
[2610.32208](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32208)
· new · primary-company · single-source

## DIFFS

[S-1] independent AI evaluation: was USD 2,000,000,000, both sides "each expect to invest at least $1 billion" (recorded 2026-10-12) -> now "at least $1 billion", Anthropic only, terms "not been finalized".
[S-1] public-benefit equity: baseline unnamed (2026-10-19) -> "beginning with our initial public offering price".
[S-1] Anthropic revenue, first tracked: "$11.6 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026", up from "$376 million" in the quarter to 2025-03-31.
[FR 2026-21786] EO 14434: terminology (2026-10-02) -> binding proposed text, 31 CFR 851.232 "Super intelligence (SI) system".
[FR 2026-21786] export controls: prohibited technology now includes "high-bandwidth memory with a memory bandwidth density greater than 2 gigabytes per second per square millimeter".
[FR 2026-21794] NHTSA post-AV-STEP row: NPRM would "allow cyan-colored ADS marker lamps" per SAE J3134. Optional, no verifier named, comments close 2026-11-25.
[FR 2026-21801] 50.43(f) is titled "Department of War"; its binding text reads "Department of Defense".
[Form D] Send Cut Send, Reno: 140,499,720 fully sold, 10 investors, "Online sheet metal fabrication service". Dropped on the sector test.
[OJ] corrigenda 24 to 26 October: zero, first such window since 2026-09-29.

## ONE QUESTION

Treasury said no benchmark can distinguish advanced models and answered by
banning the category rather than naming anyone to measure it, while the same
day Anthropic disclosed that it indemnifies its own evaluators without a cap:
does an unmeasurable property create a verifier seat or delete one, yes or no.

## PROVENANCE

Considered: 588 records from 5 collectors. F6 4 venues, F3 203 (104 EU acts
published 24 to 26 October via tools/eurlex.mjs, 99 Federal Register documents
of 26 October), F1 331 Form D and D/A filings from form.20261023.idx, F4 47
(42 arXiv cs.RO, every one dated 23 October and none 24 to 26, which is the
Monday indexing seam again; 4 OpenAI RSS items in window, 0 DeepMind, 1
Anthropic post),
F5 3.

Included: 5. Dropped as duplicate: 0. Dropped as irrelevant: 583.

Window: 72 hours, 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-26, computed from the newest file in
reports/newsletter/ per the standing instruction. The task fired on schedule.

A federal agency opened a register today and wrote into the notice that being
on it certifies nothing. The International Trade Administration launched the
U.S. Resources Management Industry Listing, applications by 11 December 2026,

days.** Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2347, published 26 October,
adds Singapore to the Article 111b(1) list under Directive 2001/83/EC.

safety standard.** arXiv 2610.35092, 26 October, tests whether a LiDAR
detector's uncertainty threshold transfers across ISO 21448 triggering
conditions. For PointPillars ensembles on KITTI and nuScenes, counted in
recorded sequences, "neither dataset held enough independent units for any
target limit". Counted in frames, transfers into far distance and into rain
returned not-applicable, and "in rain the area under the receiver operating
characteristic curve did not decrease". No pushback observed in window.

# 10 September 2026 — Thursday

Two censuses running the same method against two different populations. YC's directory
gave the capital-and-fashion read; Stanford's faculty directory gives the people read.
Both are just "scrape the public index, classify, then look at the diff over time."

> The assurance seam is no longer empty. Roughly seven to eight YC entrants in the
> 2025–26 batches are in it — Robocurve, Physical Turing, One Robot, Valgo, Risklytics,
> PRINCEPS, Hebbian Robotics, Standard Machines. That is a fact about the uncrowdedness
> axis on nodes C1, W4 and L3, and those need re-scoring before they get ranked.

> Agentic language peaked at 50.8% of the batch in Spring 2026 and has fallen two batches
> in a row, to 32.6%. Robotics went the other way over the same window. First sustained
> decline in the term since it appeared.

? Does the Fall 2026 crypto RFS request mean YC is calling a bottom, or is it a hedge?
  Five crypto companies across eleven batches against fifteen in W22+S22 alone.

? Which of the 21 Stanford orgs actually contains the people doing frontier work —
  raw faculty counts are dominated by Medicine (5,156) and that is not the signal.

Set the portal up today. Columns are the five mandate axes so a thin column reads as a
gap in the worldview rather than as a vague feeling.

Stanford pass landed the same day. The finding I did not expect:

> All 13 Stanford institutes add **zero** unique people to the faculty census. They are
> overlays on department appointments, not populations. 74.8% of faculty hold no institute
> seat at all. So "which institute is doing X" is the wrong question — the co-affiliation
> matrix is the real structure, and HAI overlaps heavily with bio and neuro (77 with Bio-X,
> 49 with Wu Tsai Neuro) while touching energy almost not at all (4 with Precourt).

> The Stanford Robotics Center roster carries appointments in Oceans, Pathology, Surgery,
> Radiology, Chemical Engineering and Civil Engineering. That is roster evidence for the
> cross-domain read, not keyword evidence.

? Four research firms size AI drug discovery 2026 between $2.9B and $24.51B — 8.4x apart.
  When that happens the number is a definition choice, not a measurement. Which means any
  deck citing one sourced TAM inherits someone's scoping decision silently. Worth a rule.

Only firm number in the whole sector: $725–800B of 2026 hyperscaler capex, company-guided,
~3x 2024, 55–60% of it to NVIDIA.

Read the people worth borrowing judgment from before designing the agents.
The line that reorganised the whole thing:

> "You can outsource your thinking, but you can't outsource your understanding."
> Karpathy, Sequoia Ascent 2026. That is the argument for two systems rather
> than one better newsletter. Flow can be delegated. Stock cannot.

> Graham's four steps are choose a field, learn to the frontier, notice the gaps,
> explore them. Most people stop before the frontier. So the flow agents serve
> step three and the stock agents serve step two, and step two is the one that
> changes what I am capable of noticing.

> EBU and BBC had 22 public service media orgs in 18 countries evaluate 3,000+
> AI assistant answers on news. 45% had a significant issue. 31% had sourcing
> problems including fabricated citations, 20% had accuracy problems. Sourcing
> failing MORE than accuracy is the real finding: a wrong fact eventually
> contradicts something I know, a wrong citation never does.

? The BIS rule of 2026-01-15 makes eligibility conditional on independent
  third-party testing to verify performance specs. Export control just grew an
  attestation layer, in the same window the EU created one for self-evolving
  safety components. Two unrelated regimes, same structural answer. What does
  the buyer of an attestation actually purchase, and is it the same thing twice?

Decisions still mine to make: funding floor, delivery channel, weekend policy,
one newsletter or five, which domain the stock side starts on, and the X list.
